question.problem:
$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 5 & 7 & 7 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the observation matrix $X$ above, where the individual observations are given in columns. Find the sample mean vector of $X.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the sample mean vector is given by

$$
m=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i},
$$

where ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ are the individual observations (columns of $X$).

From the matrix, we have that  

$$
{x}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 7\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{4}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the sample mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{1}{4}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}+{x}_{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4} \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
